A moderate 5 gives CAP 8.5 years.

overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 of the last 3 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because Federal Realty tags those two cash-flow lines only under its own extension tags (frt:CapitalExpendituresDevelopmentRedevelopment and frt:CapitalExpendituresOther in the FY2025 10-K's inline XBRL), which EDGAR companyfacts does not carry under any us-gaap candidate tag; the engine-read PaymentsForCapitalImprovements series ends at FY2019 ($82,836,000), so the override sits 3.5x that last filed value, inside the 0.1x–10x band. The engine applies this single value to every missing period (in fact FY2020–FY2025 are all assumed_zero in the preliminary history). Against the true per-year filed totals it understates FY2023 capex by $19,782,000 (flattering that year's OE), overstates FY2024 by $44,578,000 (conservative direction) and is exact for FY2025. The score is pinned to the TTM base (ttm.json), whose capex leg is this same FY2025-level spend. Excluded, deliberately: 'Acquisition of real estate' ($735,274 thousand / $273,927 thousand / $60,628 thousand for FY2025/24/23, same statement) — property acquisition (growth) spend presented separately by the filer, not capital expenditures, the same treatment as WPC/KIM/REG; and 'Leasing costs' ($25,361 thousand / $30,809 thousand / $23,510 thousand), a separate investing line the filer does not label capital expenditures.

analysis_md:
# FRT — Federal Realty Investment Trust

**STATUS: SCORED — Tier D (2026-10-20, engine release 5.5.0).** First pass-1 run. In scope (market cap $9,204,724,650 at $106.53, nasdaq_quote_api, dcf_numbers.json).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or the FY2025 10-K / Q1 2026 10-Q documents themselves — none are recomputed. Where a "true filed" figure differs from the engine's override-basis history, both are shown and labelled. Q2 2026 trading and guidance figures are from cited search results (the Q2 2026 earnings release), as noted.

## What it is
A self-administered equity REIT owning 104 predominantly mixed-use / shopping-center properties in high-barrier, affluent coastal markets — Santana Row (San Jose), Assembly Row (Boston), Pike & Rose (North Bethesda) are the flagships — with retail plus residential and office components. The model is densification and redevelopment of land it already owns, plus selective acquisitions and recycling of mature assets. It is the REIT sector's Dividend King: the Q2 2026 raise to $1.16/share quarterly ($4.64 indicated annual) was the 59th consecutive annual increase.

Current trading (Q2 2026 release, via search results): Core FFO $1.88 per diluted share, +6.8% YoY (Nareit FFO $1.88, −1.6%, only because Q2 2025 carried a one-time $13.0M / $0.15-per-share new-market-tax-credit gain); full-year 2026 Nareit and Core FFO guidance raised and tightened to $7.48–$7.56/share, +6.5% Core growth at the midpoint. Record comparable leasing of 819,000 sq ft in the quarter at +15% cash rent spreads (trailing-12-month comparable rollover +17%); portfolio 96% leased, small-shop 93.9% leased / 92.3% occupied — levels not seen since 2007. Net debt/EBITDA 5.4x, fixed-charge coverage 3.9x, liquidity $1.2B (Q2 2026 reporting). GAAP EPS is noisy by design: FY2025 net income carries a $150,111,000 gain on sale of real estate and Q2 2026 EPS fell YoY on a smaller sale gain — neither touches the OCF-based base below (the gain is backed out in the cash-flow reconciliation).

## Owner's earnings
The preliminary engine run exited 4 with DATA_GAP:capex — Federal Realty tags its two capital-expenditure cash-flow lines only under its own extension tags (`frt:CapitalExpendituresDevelopmentRedevelopment`, `frt:CapitalExpendituresOther` in the FY2025 10-K's inline XBRL), which EDGAR companyfacts does not carry under any us-gaap candidate tag the engine reads; the engine-read PaymentsForCapitalImprovements series ends at FY2019. The gap is cured by a filing-sourced override from the FY2025 10-K (bounded authority, kind "filing"; full source and reason in judgment.json, measured impact in score.json's override_impact):

- **Capex.** The 10-K's own lines are "Capital expenditures — development and redevelopment" ($179,086 thousand FY2025 / $139,534 thousand FY2024 / $214,062 thousand FY2023) and "Capital expenditures — other" ($112,252 / $107,226 / $97,058 thousand) — totals **$291,338 / $246,760 / $311,120 thousand**. The override declares $291,338,000, the median of the three filed years and also the FY2025 total; it sits 3.5x the last engine-filed value (FY2019, $82,836,000), inside the 0.1x–10x band, so no ack was needed (override_checks.capex: out_of_band false). Excluded, deliberately: "Acquisition of real estate" ($735,274 / $273,927 / $60,628 thousand) — property acquisition (growth) spend presented separately by the filer, the same treatment as WPC/KIM/REG; and "Leasing costs" ($25,361 / $30,809 / $23,510 thousand), a separate investing line the filer does not label capital expenditures. Enrichment note: statements.json's derived cash-flow rows do not reconcile to this scored chain — its generator takes the acquisition line (PaymentsToAcquireRealEstate, $735,274,000 FY2025) as its capex line, so its FY2025 FCF prints −$112,896,000 against the CSV's $331,040,000. The scored figures are the CSV / ttm.json ones; the generator's tag choice is a code fix, tracked in the engine-fix backlog.

**True filed owner's earnings (each year at its own filed capex, allocated SBC and diluted share count):**

| FY | OCF | Capex (dev. & redev. + other) | SBC | Conservative OE | OE/share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | $555,830,000 | $311,120,000 | $15,427,000 | $229,283,000 | $2.82 |
| 2024 | $574,563,000 | $246,760,000 | $17,379,000 | $310,424,000 | $3.71 |
| 2025 | $622,378,000 | $291,338,000 | $15,561,000 | $315,479,000 | $3.65 |

(OCF, SBC and share counts from financials_history.csv; capex from the 10-K lines above. The FY2025 OE/share of $3.65 reproduces the engine's base_oe_latest_per_share of $3.6512, because the override is exact for FY2025. OE positive 5 of the last 5 years — dcf_numbers.json.) True per-year median is $3.65/share. A correction to the natural shortcut: the engine's maintenance-OE series does *not* coincide with the conservative series here — it is NI-anchored (net income + D&A − capex ± working-capital), not the conservative OCF figure with capex capped at D&A, and it prints materially higher (per-share $3.29 / $4.15 / $5.64 across FY2023–25, median $4.146; FY2025 $487,581,000 vs conservative $315,479,000 — financials_history.csv). What is true is only that filed capex runs below D&A in each of the last 3 years ($311.1M vs $321.8M; $246.8M vs $342.6M; $291.3M vs $367.8M). The sweep scores the conservative OCF-based definition by rule and treats the maintenance series as a diagnostic; sized anyway (sensitivity run with the same scenarios, moat and price, base pinned to the maintenance median of $4.146/share — dcf_numbers_sensitivity_maintenance.json), it prints a weighted IRR of 7.47% and IV@15 of $40.80 — still Tier D, so the definitional choice does not carry the verdict.

- **Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q1 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct legs, saved to ttm.json):**
  - OCF: FY $622,378,000 − prior YTD $179,044,000 + current YTD $184,594,000 = **TTM $627,928,000**
  - Capex: **TTM $291,338,000** — every leg override-filled (no filed leg exists under ttm.py's candidate tags), prorated by days, so the TTM capex is exactly the FY2025 filed total. Cross-check from the filed Q1 10-Q statements (same two lines, Q1 2026 10-Q filed 2026-05-01): FY2025 $291,338 − Q1 2025 $59,029 ($31,222 + $27,807) + Q1 2026 $64,950 ($38,987 + $25,963) = $297,259 thousand of true TTM spend — the pin's capex leg is within 2% of the filed TTM spend.
  - SBC: FY $15,561,000 − prior YTD $4,112,000 + current YTD $4,537,000 = **TTM $15,986,000** (Allocated tag on every leg — ttm.json sbc_reconciled_legs)
  - Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **86,662,000**
  - **TTM OE total $320,604,000 → base OE/share $3.6995** (base_source: ttm_json). At the true filed TTM capex of $297,259 thousand the same legs give ~$3.63/share — the pin is honest to ~2%.
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) reads **$3.1813/share** — an artifact of the mechanics, disclosed rather than hidden: the single override value is applied to every gap year, so FY2024 is charged $291,338,000 instead of its own filed $246,760,000, dragging the median year down. The true per-year median is $3.65/share and the TTM pin ($3.6995) sits next to both the latest FY ($3.6512) and the true TTM (~$3.63), which is why the pin, not the distorted median, is the base. Balance sheet: net debt $4,856,187,000 on a TOTAL:LongTermDebt basis (gross debt $4,963,602,000 less cash $107,415,000, financials_history.csv); book equity $3,248,731,000. Preferred shares sit outside the engine's net debt.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: prime, supply-constrained coastal mixed-use centers with demonstrated pricing power — Q2 2026 comparable leases at +15% cash rent spreads, trailing-12-month rollover +17%, portfolio 96% leased, small-shop leased 93.9% (highest since 2007) — but measured returns are thin: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json runs 3.8% / 4.8% / 5.8% / 4.4% / 4.9% / 5.9% for FY2020–FY2025, well below wide-moat territory (partly a depreciated-cost REIT book effect, but the level is the level); the filer reports no gross-margin split (fundamentals.json gross margin is null), and operating margin swings 35–49% with sale gains.
- FOR: Irreplaceable high-barrier coastal locations — 104 mixed-use / shopping-center properties (Santana Row, Assembly Row, Pike & Rose) in affluent, supply-constrained markets; proven pricing power — Q2 2026 comparable leases at +15% cash rent spreads, trailing-12-month comparable rollover +17%, the highest in over 10 years; occupancy and demand depth — portfolio 96% leased, small-shop 93.9% leased / 92.3% occupied (levels not seen since 2007), record 819,000 sq ft of comparable leasing in Q2 2026; durability through cycles — 59 consecutive years of dividend increases (longest in the REIT sector), raised FY2026 Core FFO guidance to $7.48–$7.56/share (+6.5% at midpoint).
- AGAINST: Low measured returns on capital — roic_proxy only ~4–6% across FY2020–FY2025 in fundamentals.json; capital intensity — filed capital expenditures run $246.8–311.1M/yr, roughly half of operating cash flow, and development/redevelopment must be re-earned continuously; growth partly bought, not only earned — $735,274,000 of real-estate acquisitions in FY2025 funded with debt and share issuance (shares_diluted 81,313,000 in FY2023 to 86,405,000 in FY2025, financials_history.csv); leverage and rate exposure — net debt $4,856,187,000, 5.4x net debt/EBITDA in Q2 2026 reporting, plus retail-tenant and anchor-transition risk.
- CAP at moat 5 = **8.5 years** (dcf_numbers.json): growth holds 2 years, then fades to the 2.5% terminal rate over the CAP.

## DCF — final run (engine release 5.5.0, 2026-10-20)
**Growth-start sanity check (mandatory).** The engine's blended start is 5.24% (g_blend in dcf_numbers.json): adjusted components are rev CAGR 5y 6.51%, rev CAGR 3y 3.60%, latest rev YoY 3.98% (each after the −2.38pp share-count adjustment) and OE/share CAGR 9.17% — the OE component runs hot because the flat override capex makes historical OE track OCF growth. Against actual prints — FY2025 revenue +6.36% (financials_history.csv), TTM revenue +7.43% YoY (fundamentals.json), comparable POI growth +4.7% in Q1 2026 (search results) and FY2026 Core FFO guided to +6.5% at the midpoint — a 5.24% base start sits inside the observed range, between property-level POI growth and the FFO guide, so the default offsets were kept (−12 / −5 / 0 / +5 / +12pp). The bull (+10.24%) and super-bull (+17.24%) starts sit above every recent print by construction — they are tails that require the rent-spread compounding to persist while capex plateaus — and even the super-bull IV@15% of $69.53 is 35% below the $106.53 price: **the price, not the growth debate, decides this verdict.** Probabilities default 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −6.8% | 0.75 | $15.44 | 4.10% |
| Bear | 25% | +0.2% | 0.90 | $24.85 | 5.35% |
| Base | 30% | +5.2% | 1.00 | $34.00 | 6.58% |
| Bull | 25% | +10.2% | 1.10 | $45.98 | 8.17% |
| Super bull | 10% | +17.2% | 1.25 | $69.53 | 11.06% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $36.40 (−66% vs price), IV@20% $25.53, IV@25% $19.57, weighted IRR 6.94%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 3.47%, terminal value 19.1% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.50x, net debt 15.2x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:capex** (preliminary run): cured by the filing-sourced capex override above (FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement, extension-tagged lines). data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run; the override is registered with measured impact.
- **CAPEX_COVERAGE_LOW** (preliminary run only): an artifact of the same gap — coverage read 0% because capex was assumed zero. On the filed figures, capex is 97% / 72% / 79% of D&A in FY2023/24/25, above the 50% test in every year; the flag does not fire in the final run. The investing section was reconciled line by line: the only other investing outflows are acquisitions of real estate and leasing costs, both excluded with reasons stated above.
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended ~10 months ago): resolved by construction — ttm.py was run (ttm.json saved) and the final pass used the `--ttm` pin; the TTM legs are quoted in full above and the capex leg was cross-checked against filed Q1 10-Q spend (~$3.63/share true TTM vs the $3.6995 pin). Note companyfacts stops at Q1 2026 — the Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-31) is not yet in companyfacts (fundamentals.json warning) — so the freshest filing-direct TTM is through Q1 2026; the Q2 2026 release figures (Core FFO $1.88/share, guidance raised) show the same trend continuing, nothing that lifts a 3.47% OE yield toward a 15% hurdle.
- **SBC_TAG_RECONCILED**: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense exceeds ShareBasedCompensation in every year FY2016–FY2025 (+13.2% down to +6.5%; FY2025 $15,561,000 vs $14,608,000) and was used throughout, including all three TTM legs (ttm.json sbc_reconciled_legs). The Allocated figure is the filer's full stock-compensation cost; SBC is in any case ~2.5% of OCF, so the choice is immaterial to the verdict.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: the filing override above; kind "filing," in band (3.5x the last engine-filed value), unblocks the tier — and the tier it unblocks is D, while the zero-fill preliminary base printed $6.6676/share, so the override is doing the verdict no favors.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.50x super-bear): real — capex lumpiness (filed spend swung $246.8–311.1M across the last 3 years, and development starts of $400–500M are planned per Q2 2026 reporting) makes the OE path genuinely wide. Confidence is graded **low** and the verdict is sized to the conservative end. The scenario probabilities stay at the defaults (10/25/30/25/10) deliberately: the $400–500M starts figure is a pipeline number, not a spend schedule — filed development/redevelopment spend ran $214.1M / $139.5M / $179.1M across FY2023–25 inside capex totals of $311.1M / $246.8M / $291.3M — the TTM base already charges capex at the $291.3M level, and the scenario growth offsets (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp) already span the capex-driven OE swing; shifting probability mass bearish on top of that would charge the same program twice. The uncertainty is carried in the IV range and the low confidence instead.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 15.2x normalized OE): the denominator is OE after charging all capital expenditures, the most conservative lens; on the REIT lens the same balance sheet is 5.4x net debt/EBITDA with 3.9x fixed-charge coverage and $1.2B of liquidity (Q2 2026 reporting). Leverage is still real — $4,856,187,000 of net debt against $320,604,000 of TTM OE means a capex-heavy, low-OCF year squeezes OE fast, which is what the bear cases (35% combined probability) carry.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Real Estate): accepted in full — the OE/capex DCF fits REITs poorly, because a large share of the $291.3M annual spend is development and redevelopment at yields (growth capex), not upkeep, and the sweep's conservative definition charges all of it. Confidence is graded **low** and the tier reads as "fails the standardized conservative OE screen at this price," not "the centers lose cash." On the REIT lens the buyer pays ~14x guided FY2026 Core FFO of $7.48–$7.56/share for ~6.5% guided growth, and the $4.64 indicated dividend (62% of FY2025 Nareit FFO per the filer's supplemental) is covered by FFO but not by owner's earnings after all capital spend (FY2025 dividends paid $388,058,000 vs conservative OE $315,479,000, both from the FY2025 10-K / table above). The sector lens softens the D; it does not overturn it. No tier override — peer REITs scored on this screen (REG, KIM, UDR at D; WPC at C) took none, and the float-capitalization notch is an insurer/financials rule that does not apply to an OCF base with no policyholder or fund flows.

## Thoughts / method range
- The honest tension is the capex line. Charging all $291.3M of development, redevelopment and other capital expenditures against OE treats a growth program as upkeep; charging none of it (the preliminary zero-fill) printed a $6.6676/share base. Unlike REG (capex above D&A), FRT's filed capex runs *below* D&A every year. The one kinder series is the engine's NI-anchored maintenance OE (median $4.146/share, sized in the sensitivity run above: 7.47%, still D). Beyond it, the only larger line is the acquisition line ($735.3M in FY2025), which no worker convention charges to OE.
- Method range, all on filed figures: engine normalized median $3.1813/share (override-mechanics artifact, disclosed above) → still Tier D; true per-year median $3.65/share → Tier D; TTM pin $3.6995 → 6.94% weighted IRR, Tier D; true TTM ~$3.63/share → Tier D. **Every defensible base gives Tier D.**
- What the price is actually paying for: cap-rate value on irreplaceable coastal real estate and a 59-year dividend record, neither of which an owner's-earnings DCF at a 15% hurdle credits. That is a legitimate way to own this asset; it is not a 15% owner's-earnings return at $106.53.

## Verdict
**Tier D — sized to the conservative end.** A genuinely high-quality, moderately moated REIT (moat 5/10) whose TTM owner's earnings of $3.6995/share support a 6.94% weighted IRR at $106.53. It clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$36 (weighted IV@15% $36.40), 20% below ~$26 (IV@20% $25.53) and 25% below ~$20 (IV@25% $19.57). Confidence low (sector model misfit, wide scenario spread).
